data.name: Avinash
data.gender_notes: Avinash is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Avinash translates to 'absence of sins' in Sanskrit. It is derived from the Sanskrit words 'avinā' (without) and 'nāsh' (sins). In Hindu mythology, Avinash is considered a synonym for Moksha, or liberation from the cycle of birth and death. The name Avinash carries the meaning “Absence of Sins” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Avinash usually hope their child will grow to embody absence of sins and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Liberation from the cycle of birth and death
data.etymology: Avinash belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Absence of Sins.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Avinash total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Avinash' is deeply rooted in Hinduism, reflecting the cultural values of self-discipline, morality, and the pursuit of spiritual growth. It is a name worth aspiring to, as it symbolizes the goal of a virtuous and sinless life.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu philosophy, the attainment of Avinash signifies the ultimate goal of spiritual journey. It represents the absolution of all karmas, achieving inner peace, and freeing the soul from the cycle of birth and death. Avinash is a reminder of the importance of living a righteous life, adhering to the principles of Dharma, leading to a life of Moksha or enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Avinash, meaning "without a trace" or "unending", symbolizes the purified soul that leaves no footprints of worldly desires or attachments behind, steadfastly moving towards spiritual enlightenment.

vedic_reference.note: The name Avinash is derived from the Sanskrit word 'अविनाश' (Avinaash) which means 'that which is not to be destroyed, imperishable'. It is also the name of the Hindu deity Shiva, who is often referred to as 'अविनाशकर' (Avinashkar), the lord of Avinaash, the imperishable.

historical_references.reference: Avinash was the name of a well-known Hindu sage and philosopher born around the 11th century CE. He was a disciple of the philosopher Shankara and is considered one of the major contributors to the philosophical tradition of Advaita Vedanta.
historical_references.context: Advaita Vedanta is a philosophical tradition that emphasizes non-dualism or the oneness of the universe and the individual self. It was influenced by the Upanishads and the Bhagavad Gita.

historical_references.reference: Avinash also appears in the Hindu epic Mahabharata as the name of a sage who was a close friend of the great warrior Bhima. Avinash is said to have blessed Bhima with invulnerability to weapons and the power to assume any form.
historical_references.context: The Mahabharata is a Sanskrit epic poem that tells the story of the Kurukshetra war between two branches of a royal family, the Pandavas and the Kauravas.

On Medium, they often publish articles on the latest technology trends and startup advice.
